records.source: Ἀγαπητοί, μὴ παντὶ πνεύματι πιστεύετε, ἀλλὰ δοκιμάζετε τὰ πνεύματα εἰ ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν, ὅτι πολλοὶ ψευδοπροφῆται ἐξεληλύθασιν εἰς τὸν κόσμον.
records.gloss: Beloved, not every spirit believe, but test the spirits whether from God they are, because many false prophets have gone out into the world.
pieces: Dear friends, do not believe just any spirit; test the spirits to find out whether they are from God, because many false prophets have gone out and are now in the world.

L.1: Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits [to see] whether they are from God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world.

R.1: Dear friends, do not believe every spirit that speaks through a prophet. Test them to find out whether they really come from God. You need to do this, because many false prophets have gone out into the world.

decisions.choice: dear ones: a warm address to the readers, built on the word for love
alternatives: those loved by God (as a title)
decisions.reason: Ἀγαπητοί comes from the verb ἀγαπάω (love) and is the letter's usual affectionate address (2:7; 3:2, 21; 4:7, 11). In 4:7 and 4:11 it opens a call to love, so the link with love is felt there.

decisions.choice: spirit: the spiritual power that speaks through a prophet
decisions.reason: The spirits are tested by what is said (4:2-3), and each one is either the Spirit of God or the spirit of the antichrist (4:3, 6). Every prophet claims to speak by a spirit; testing the spirits means testing what the prophets say. Compare 1 Corinthians 12:10 and 14:32.

decisions.choice: a standing rule: do not go on believing every spirit
decisions.reason: A negative with the present imperative forbids a habit or continuing practice. The readers are not to accept a message simply because it claims the Spirit; the companion command to test is also present: keep testing.

decisions.choice: false prophets: people who claim to speak for God when he has not sent them
decisions.reason: The law of Moses gave tests for prophets (Deuteronomy 13:1-5; 18:20-22), and Jesus warned that false prophets would come (Matthew 24:11, 24). "Have gone out" uses the same verb as 2:19, where those who left the community "went out from us"; the letter seems to connect the two.

decisions.choice: the world: human society that does not know God, where these prophets now find a hearing
decisions.reason: Key term. The sense is set by 4:5: they belong to the world and the world listens to them (compare 2:15-17; 5:19).

decisions.choice: Beloved (L); Dear friends (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Beloved" is now heard mostly in church or as old-fashioned; "Dear friends" is the natural warm address. Literal keeps "Beloved" so the reader can see that the word is built on "love" (meaning decision m1). The same choice is made in 4:7 and 4:11.

decisions.choice: every spirit that speaks through a prophet
decisions.reason: Readable says what the spirits are in this passage (meaning decision m2), since "spirit" alone gives a young reader no picture.

decisions.choice: have gone out and are now in the world
alternatives: have gone out into the world
decisions.reason: The perfect tense says they went out and are now at work; Balanced spells out the second half. Literal and Readable keep the plain wording.

records.heading: Testing the spirits

records.source: ἐν τούτῳ γινώσκετε τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ· πᾶν πνεῦμα ὃ ὁμολογεῖ Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἐν σαρκὶ ἐληλυθότα ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν, καὶ πᾶν πνεῦμα ὃ μὴ ὁμολογεῖ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐκ ἔστιν· καὶ τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ τοῦ ἀντιχρίστου, ὃ ἀκηκόατε ὅτι ἔρχεται, καὶ νῦν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ἐστὶν ἤδη.
records.gloss: By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses Jesus Christ in flesh having come from God is, \v 3 and every spirit that not confesses the Jesus from God not is; and this is the [spirit] of the antichrist, which you have heard that it is coming, and now in the world it is already.
pieces: Here is how you recognize the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} as one who has come in the flesh is from God,
and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God. This is the spirit of the antichrist; you have heard that it is coming, and now it is already in the world.

L.2: By this you know the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} having come in [the] flesh is from God,
L.3: and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not from God; and this is the [spirit] of the antichrist, which you have heard is coming, and now it is in the world already.

R.2: This is how you can recognize the Spirit of God. Every spirit that openly says that Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} came as a real human being is from God.
R.3: But every spirit that will not say this about Jesus is not from God. That is the spirit of the antichrist. You have heard that it was coming, and now it is already in the world.

decisions.choice: a statement: this is how you know
alternatives: a command: know (recognize) the Spirit of God by this
decisions.reason: The form γινώσκετε can be a statement or a command. The parallel at the end of the section, "from this we know" (4:6), favors a statement. Either way the sentence gives the test.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of God: the Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: Against the many spirits of 4:1, there is one Spirit of God, who is also called the Spirit of truth (4:6) and whom God has given to believers (3:24; 4:13).

decisions.choice: confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh: the participle states what is confessed about him
alternatives: confesses Jesus as the Christ who has come in the flesh
confesses Jesus Christ, who has come in the flesh (the participle only describing him)
decisions.reason: After a verb of saying or confessing, an object followed by a participle gives the content of what is said. The stress falls on "in flesh": the test is not whether a spirit names Jesus Christ but whether it confesses that he came as a real human being. The perfect ἐληλυθότα says he came and remains the one who came in the flesh. 2 John 7 states the same confession with a present participle.

decisions.choice: in flesh: a real human body and human life
alternatives: the heavenly Christ resting on the man Jesus for a time
decisions.reason: The confession matches John 1:14 ("the Word became flesh") and the eyewitness claim of 1:1-3 (what we heard, saw and touched). The letter does not name the false teachers. It is well known that some in the early second century taught that Christ only seemed to have a body; whether this letter faces exactly that teaching, or one that separated the divine Christ from the human Jesus (compare 2:22), is not certain. The confession answers both.

decisions.choice: does not confess Jesus (all known Greek manuscripts; SBLGNT)
alternatives: "annuls Jesus" or "separates Jesus" (λύει instead of μὴ ὁμολογεῖ)
does not confess Jesus Christ as having come in the flesh (later manuscripts filling out the phrase from 4:2)
decisions.reason: Every known Greek manuscript of the letter has "does not confess". But a reading "which annuls (or dissolves) Jesus" was known early: it is in the Latin Vulgate (solvit), it is quoted by some early church writers, and a note in the margin of minuscule 1739 says Origen knew it. It reads like a sharpened interpretation aimed at teachers who split Jesus from the Christ. Many later manuscripts also fill out the confession from 4:2 ("Jesus Christ has come in the flesh"). The SBLGNT follows the oldest Greek text. A reviewer must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: this Jesus: the one just confessed as come in the flesh
alternatives: refusing to speak of Jesus at all
decisions.reason: The article points back to the Jesus of the previous clause. Not confessing him means refusing the confession just given, not simply never mentioning his name.

decisions.choice: the spirit of the antichrist: the neuter article stands for "spirit"
alternatives: the work or doing of the antichrist
decisions.reason: τὸ is neuter, like πνεῦμα; the whole passage is about spirits, so the word to be supplied is "spirit".

decisions.choice: the antichrist: the opponent of Christ expected at the end, whose spirit is already at work
decisions.reason: The readers had been taught that the antichrist was coming (2:18). John says many antichrists have already come (2:18, 22; 2 John 7): the spirit of the expected opponent is already speaking through false prophets. The prefix means against, and can also mean in place of.

decisions.choice: confesses (L, B); openly says (R)
decisions.reason: To confess here is to declare publicly what one holds true and stands by, not to admit wrongdoing. Literal and Balanced keep the church word "confess"; Readable says plainly what it means. The same choice is made in 4:15.

decisions.choice: as one who has come in the flesh (B); came as a real human being (R)
alternatives: that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the object-and-participle shape of meaning decision m3 so the confession stays about the person. Readable explains "in the flesh" (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: the [spirit] of the antichrist (L); the spirit of the antichrist (B, R)
decisions.reason: English needs the noun the Greek leaves understood (meaning decision m7).

decisions.choice: antichrist, with no christos setting
decisions.reason: The christos setting gives a choice for the title Christ. "Antichrist" is one established word, and "anti-Messiah" is not standard usage; meaning decision m8 says what the word means.

decisions.choice: will not say this about Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable makes explicit that the refusal is of the confession just given (meaning decision m6).

records.source: ὑμεῖς ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστε, τεκνία, καὶ νενικήκατε αὐτούς, ὅτι μείζων ἐστὶν ὁ ἐν ὑμῖν ἢ ὁ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ·
records.gloss: You from God are, little children, and you have overcome them, because greater is the [one] in you than the [one] in the world;
pieces: As for you, dear children, you belong to God, and you have already won the victory over them, because the one in you is greater than the one in the world.

L.4: You are from God, little children, and you have overcome them, because greater is the one in you than the one in the world.

R.4: But you, dear children, belong to God. You have already won the fight against these false prophets, because God, who lives in you, is greater than the devil, who is in the world.

decisions.choice: you, in contrast with the false prophets
decisions.reason: The pronoun is emphatic and sets the readers against the false prophets of 4:1-3 and "they" in 4:5.

decisions.choice: from God: their life comes from God and they belong to him
decisions.reason: Said of people, being "from" God or "from" the world names where their life comes from and whom they belong to (3:10; 4:5-6; 5:19).

decisions.choice: little children: an affectionate address to all the readers
decisions.reason: John calls all his readers this (2:1, 12, 28; 3:7, 18; 5:21).

decisions.choice: you have overcome them: a victory already won and still standing; "them" are the false prophets
decisions.reason: The perfect speaks of a victory won and lasting. "Them" is masculine and points back to the false prophets of 4:1; the readers have overcome them by not being led astray (2:13-14, 26-27; 5:4-5).

decisions.choice: the one in you: God, living in believers by his Spirit
decisions.reason: The nearby verses speak of God remaining in us and giving us his Spirit (3:24; 4:12-13, 15-16). The letter speaks of God, Christ and the Spirit in believers so closely that the alternatives say much the same.

decisions.choice: the one in the world: the devil, working through the spirit of the antichrist
decisions.reason: Elsewhere the letter calls him the devil and the evil one, and says the whole world lies in his power (3:8, 10; 5:19).

decisions.choice: belong to God (B, R); are from God (L)
alternatives: are from God at every level
decisions.reason: Said of people, "from God" can sound like "sent from God". "Belong to" gives meaning decision m2. The same choice is made for people in 4:5-6.

decisions.choice: dear children; have already won the victory over them (B); have already won the fight against (R)
decisions.reason: "Little children" can sound as if young children were meant (meaning decision m3). "Already" gives the force of the perfect (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: these false prophets; God, who lives in you; the devil
alternatives: them; the one in you; the one in the world
decisions.reason: Readable names who is meant (meaning decisions m4-m6).

records.source: αὐτοὶ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου εἰσίν· διὰ τοῦτο ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου λαλοῦσιν καὶ ὁ κόσμος αὐτῶν ἀκούει.
records.gloss: They from the world are; because of this from the world they speak and the world them hears.
pieces: They belong to the world, so what they say comes from the world, and the world listens to them.

L.5: They are from the world; because of this they speak from the world, and the world listens to them.

R.5: Those false prophets belong to the world. That is why they talk the way the world talks, and the world listens to them.

decisions.choice: they: the false prophets
decisions.reason: The emphatic pronoun answers "you" in 4:4 and points back to the false prophets of 4:1.

decisions.choice: the world: human society organized without God
decisions.reason: Key term. As in 2:15-17 and 5:19: the world here is humanity that does not know God, and it welcomes those who speak its language.

decisions.choice: they speak from the world: what they say has its source in the world's way of thinking
decisions.reason: The phrase names where the speech comes from, not its topic. Compare John 3:31: the one from the earth speaks from the earth.

decisions.choice: listens to: hears with acceptance
decisions.reason: With the person in the genitive the verb means to listen to and accept, as again in 4:6.

decisions.choice: what they say comes from the world (B); they talk the way the world talks (R)
decisions.reason: "Speak from the world" is unclear in English; Balanced and Readable give the sense of meaning decision m3.

decisions.choice: belong to the world
decisions.reason: As "belong to God" in 4:4.

records.source: ἡμεῖς ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐσμεν· ὁ γινώσκων τὸν θεὸν ἀκούει ἡμῶν, ὃς οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐκ ἀκούει ἡμῶν.
records.gloss: We from God are; the [one] knowing God hears us, [he] who not is from God not hears us.
pieces: We belong to God. Whoever knows God listens to us, and whoever does not belong to God does not listen to us.

L.6: We are from God; the one who knows God listens to us; whoever is not from God does not listen to us.

R.6: We belong to God. People who know God listen to us. People who do not belong to God will not listen to us.

decisions.choice: we: the witnesses who carry the message heard from the beginning
decisions.reason: "We" is set against "they" (4:5), and listening to "us" is the test. That fits the eyewitnesses who saw and heard and passed the message on (1:1-5; 4:14), and with them all who hold to what was heard from the beginning (2:24). The readers are called "you" in 4:4; in the next sentence "we know" seems to include them.

decisions.choice: knows God: knows him personally, as one who belongs to him
decisions.reason: In this letter knowing God is a relationship shown in obedience and love (2:3-4; 4:7-8).

decisions.choice: listens to: hears with acceptance
decisions.reason: As in 4:5.

decisions.choice: belong to God
decisions.reason: As in 4:4.

records.source: ἐκ τούτου γινώσκομεν τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς πλάνης.
records.gloss: From this we know the Spirit of the truth and the spirit of the error.
pieces: That is how we tell the Spirit of truth from the spirit of falsehood.

L.6: From this we know the Spirit of truth and the spirit of error.

R.6: This is how we can tell the Spirit of truth from the spirit that leads people astray.

decisions.choice: from this: from who listens to the message and who does not
decisions.reason: Nothing follows in the sentence, so τούτου points back to 4:6a, and through it to the confession of 4:2-3.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of truth: the Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: Jesus calls the Holy Spirit "the Spirit of truth" (John 14:17; 15:26; 16:13), and this letter says the Spirit is the truth (5:6). It is the same Spirit of God as in 4:2.

decisions.choice: the spirit of error: the spirit that leads people astray
decisions.reason: πλάνη means wandering from the way, and so deception. Its verb is used of those who lead the readers astray (2:26; 3:7). It is the spirit of the antichrist of 4:3.

decisions.choice: two spirits set against each other
decisions.reason: Jewish writings of the time also spoke this way: the Community Rule among the Dead Sea Scrolls speaks of a spirit of truth and a spirit of deceit at work in people. The letter shares the language but grounds it in the confession of Jesus.

decisions.choice: error (L); falsehood (B); that leads people astray (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the familiar "error"; Balanced pairs "falsehood" with "truth"; Readable says what the spirit does (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: tell ... from
decisions.reason: The point is to tell the two spirits apart; "tell one from the other" says so.

records.source: Ἀγαπητοί, ἀγαπῶμεν ἀλλήλους, ὅτι ἡ ἀγάπη ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἀγαπῶν ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ γεγέννηται καὶ γινώσκει τὸν θεόν.
records.gloss: Beloved, let us love one another, because the love from God is, and everyone loving from God has been born and knows God.
pieces: Dear friends, let us keep loving one another, for love has its source in God; everyone who loves is born of God and knows {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.7: Beloved, let us love one another, because love is from God, and everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God.

R.7: Dear friends, let us love each other, because love comes from God. Everyone who loves is God's child and knows God.

decisions.choice: let us love: a call to keep on loving
decisions.reason: In the present tense the call and the statement have the same form. The address "Beloved" and the "ought" of 4:11 show a call. The present tense asks for love as a lasting way of life.

decisions.choice: love: the self-giving love God has shown
decisions.reason: The passage defines love by what God did: he sent his Son (4:9-10). The article marks love as a known reality, the love the passage is about.

decisions.choice: new birth comes first; love is its sign
alternatives: loving makes a person a child of God
any human affection proves birth from God
decisions.reason: The perfect "has been born" puts the birth before the loving: love shows that God has given new life, as in 2:29, 3:9 and 5:1. The love meant is love for one another as this passage describes it (4:7, 11, 20-21), not any affection at all.

decisions.choice: knows God personally
decisions.reason: As in 4:6.

decisions.choice: Dear friends
decisions.reason: As in 4:1.

decisions.choice: let us keep loving; is born of God
alternatives: let us love; has been born of God
decisions.reason: "Keep" gives the present tense of meaning decision m1. "Is born of God" states the lasting result of the perfect; Literal keeps "has been born".

decisions.choice: is God's child
decisions.reason: Readable gives the plain sense of the birth image: such a person has been made a child of God (3:1-2).

records.heading: God is love

records.source: ὁ μὴ ἀγαπῶν οὐκ ἔγνω τὸν θεόν, ὅτι ὁ θεὸς ἀγάπη ἐστίν.
records.gloss: The [one] not loving not knew God, because the God love is.
pieces: The one who does not love has never known God, for God is love.

L.8: The one who does not love has not known God, because God is love.

R.8: Anyone who does not love has never really known God, because God is love.

decisions.choice: has never come to know God
decisions.reason: The past tense, after the present "knows" of 4:7, looks at the whole of a life: the person who does not love never came to know God at all.

decisions.choice: God is love: love belongs to God's very nature, and everything he does is loving
alternatives: love is God (reversing subject and predicate)
God loves (only an action, not what he is)
decisions.reason: θεὸς has the article and is the subject; ἀγάπη has none and says what God is. So the sentence cannot be turned round to say that love is God, or that all love is divine. Nor does it reduce God to a feeling: the next verses define the love by what God did, sending his Son (4:9-10). It is not the whole of what can be said of God, who is also light (1:5) and spirit (John 4:24). The sentence comes again in 4:16.

decisions.choice: because: the reason not loving shows not knowing
decisions.reason: Since God is love, to know him is to be changed by his love; a life without love shows that this has not happened.

decisions.choice: has never known (B); has never really known (R)
decisions.reason: "Never" gives the sense of meaning decision m1; Literal keeps "has not known".

records.source: ἐν τούτῳ ἐφανερώθη ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν ἡμῖν, ὅτι τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ τὸν μονογενῆ ἀπέσταλκεν ὁ θεὸς εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἵνα ζήσωμεν δι’ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: In this was revealed the love of God in us, that the Son of him the only one has sent God into the world so that we might live through him.
pieces: This is how God's love was made visible among us: God has sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} one and only Son into the world, so that through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} we may have life.

L.9: In this the love of God was revealed among us, that God has sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, the one and only, into the world so that we might live through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.9: God made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} love plain for us to see. He sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} one and only Son into the world so that we could have real life through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: in this: points ahead to the sending of the Son
decisions.reason: The ὅτι clause says what "this" is.

decisions.choice: was revealed: shown openly, in an event that happened
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the life that appeared (1:2) and of the Son who appeared (3:5, 8). God's love was shown in history, in the coming of the Son.

decisions.choice: among us: shown to us, in what happened to us
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "in us", but here it names those to whom and for whom the love was shown; the sending of the Son into the world is the showing.

decisions.choice: one and only, unique
decisions.reason: As in John 1:14, 1:18 and 3:16: μονογενής is built from μόνος (only) and γένος (kind), not from γεννάω (beget). Hebrews 11:17 uses it of Isaac, who was not Abraham's only son. "Only begotten" came through the Latin unigenitus.

decisions.choice: has sent: a sending whose effect still stands
decisions.reason: The perfect looks at the sending and its lasting result; 4:10 tells the same event with a simple past.

decisions.choice: live: have the life of God, eternal life, through the Son
decisions.reason: In this letter life is eternal life, given in the Son (1:2; 5:11-12). Those who had been in death pass into life (3:14). Compare John 3:16 and 10:10.

decisions.choice: his Son, the one and only (L); his one and only Son (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same wording as John 3:16 (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: may have life (B); could have real life (R)
decisions.reason: "Live" alone can sound like staying alive. "Have life" and "real life" point to the life of meaning decision m6. Literal keeps "live".

decisions.choice: God made his love plain for us to see. He sent ...
alternatives: In this the love of God was revealed among us, that ...
decisions.reason: Readable makes the forward-pointing "in this" two short sentences.

records.source: ἐν τούτῳ ἐστὶν ἡ ἀγάπη, οὐχ ὅτι ἡμεῖς ἠγαπήκαμεν τὸν θεόν, ἀλλ’ ὅτι αὐτὸς ἠγάπησεν ἡμᾶς καὶ ἀπέστειλεν τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ἱλασμὸν περὶ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν.
records.gloss: In this is the love, not that we have loved God but that he loved us and sent the Son of him [as] a propitiation concerning the sins of us.
pieces: This is where love is found: not in our having loved God, but in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loving us and sending {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son to be the atoning sacrifice for our sins.

L.10: In this is love, not that we have loved God, but that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loved us and sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son [as] an atoning sacrifice for our sins.

R.10: This is what love really is. It is not that we loved God. It is that God loved us and sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son to be the sacrifice that takes away our sins.

decisions.choice: in this is love: love itself is defined by what God did
alternatives: this is one example of love
decisions.reason: ἐν τούτῳ points ahead to the two ὅτι clauses. With the article, ἀγάπη is love itself, real love: it is known from God's act, not from ours.

decisions.choice: we ... he: the love began with God, not with us
decisions.reason: Both pronouns are emphatic. The contrast is taken up again in 4:19: he loved us first.

decisions.choice: atoning sacrifice: the sacrifice by which sins are dealt with and God's judgment on them is turned away
alternatives: propitiation (a sacrifice that turns away God's anger)
expiation (a sacrifice that wipes out sin)
decisions.reason: The same word, in the same sense, as in 2:2 (see the decision there). In the Greek Old Testament it belongs to the language of atonement for sin (Leviticus 25:9; Numbers 5:8; Ezekiel 44:27). Whether it stresses turning away God's anger or wiping out sin is debated; the letter speaks both of sin cleansed (1:7, 9) and of the Son as advocate with the Father (2:1). Here the sacrifice comes from God's own love: it is God's gift, not something that wins over an unwilling God. "Atoning sacrifice" keeps both sides.

decisions.choice: for our sins: to deal with them
decisions.reason: The preposition means concerning, with regard to: the sacrifice is about our sins and deals with them.

decisions.choice: This is where love is found: not in our having loved God, but in his loving us and sending
alternatives: This is love: not that we loved God, but that he loved us and sent
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the two "that" clauses into matching phrases so the contrast between our love and his stays clear.

decisions.choice: atoning sacrifice
decisions.reason: "Propitiation" and "expiation" are unfamiliar to most readers and each takes one side of the debate in meaning decision m3. "Atoning sacrifice" is plain and keeps both, as in 2:2.

decisions.choice: the sacrifice that takes away our sins
decisions.reason: Readable avoids "atoning". "Takes away" echoes John 1:29, but says less than meaning decision m3 (it leaves out the turning away of judgment); a reviewer should weigh it.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God (the subject of 4:9).

records.source: ἀγαπητοί, εἰ οὕτως ὁ θεὸς ἠγάπησεν ἡμᾶς, καὶ ἡμεῖς ὀφείλομεν ἀλλήλους ἀγαπᾶν.
records.gloss: Beloved, if so God loved us, also we ought one another to love.
pieces: Dear friends, since this is how God loved us, we too should love one another.

L.11: Beloved, if God loved us in this way, we also ought to love one another.

R.11: Dear friends, God loved us like this. So we should love each other too.

decisions.choice: if, meaning since: the condition is true
decisions.reason: The "if" assumes the fact just stated (4:9-10) and argues from it.

decisions.choice: in this way: by sending his Son
decisions.reason: οὕτως means "thus, in this way", pointing back to 4:9-10, as in John 3:16. The way God loved also shows how great his love is, but the word points first to the manner.

decisions.choice: ought: we are under obligation, as people who owe a debt
decisions.reason: The verb means to owe. Having received such love, we owe love to one another (compare 2:6; 3:16).

decisions.choice: Dear friends
decisions.reason: As in 4:1.

decisions.choice: ought (L); should (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Should" is the ordinary word for an obligation; "must" would sound like a rule rather than a debt of love.

records.source: θεὸν οὐδεὶς πώποτε τεθέαται· ἐὰν ἀγαπῶμεν ἀλλήλους, ὁ θεὸς ἐν ἡμῖν μένει καὶ ἡ ἀγάπη αὐτοῦ ἐν ἡμῖν τετελειωμένη ἐστιν.
records.gloss: God no one ever has seen; if we love one another, God in us remains and the love of him in us having been perfected is.
pieces: No one has ever seen God. If we love one another, God remains in us, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} love has reached completion in us.

L.12: No one has ever seen God; if we love one another, God remains in us, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} love has been perfected in us.

R.12: No one has ever seen God. But if we love each other, God remains in us, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} love has done its full work in us.

decisions.choice: no one has ever seen God: as John 1:18
decisions.reason: The sentence echoes John 1:18 almost word for word. There the unseen God is made known by the Son; here he is seen at work when believers love one another. θεὸν comes first for emphasis.

decisions.choice: remains: a lasting, living union
decisions.reason: As in John 6:56 and 15:4-10. This letter speaks often of God remaining in us and us in him (3:24; 4:13, 15-16).

decisions.choice: his love: God's love for us
decisions.reason: The passage is about God's love for us (4:9-11). That love reaches its goal when it goes on in our love for one another. The phrase could also mean our love for God, as perhaps in 2:5.

decisions.choice: has been brought to completion: has reached its goal
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring to its end or goal. God's love reaches what it was meant for when it is lived out among his people; it does not mean they are without sin (1:8). The same word is used in 2:5 and 4:17-18.

decisions.choice: has been perfected (L); has reached completion (B); has done its full work (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "perfected" so the word family of 4:12, 17-18 can be seen. Balanced and Readable avoid "perfect", which suggests flawlessness (meaning decision m4).

records.source: Ἐν τούτῳ γινώσκομεν ὅτι ἐν αὐτῷ μένομεν καὶ αὐτὸς ἐν ἡμῖν, ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ πνεύματος αὐτοῦ δέδωκεν ἡμῖν.
records.gloss: By this we know that in him we remain and he in us, because from the Spirit of him he has given to us.
pieces: This is how we know that we remain in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} remains in us: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given us from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own Spirit.

L.13: By this we know that we remain in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} in us: because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given us of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit.

R.13: This is how we know that we remain in God and God remains in us: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given us {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit.

decisions.choice: by this: the gift of the Spirit, named in the ὅτι clause
decisions.reason: The ὅτι clause tells what "this" is, as in 3:24: "by this we know that he remains in us, from the Spirit he has given us". Love for one another (4:12) is the outward sign, the Spirit the inward one.

decisions.choice: him, he: God
decisions.reason: God is the subject of 4:12 and 4:15-16.

decisions.choice: from his Spirit: God has given us a share in his Spirit
alternatives: he has given us his Spirit (all of him)
decisions.reason: The preposition takes a part from a whole. It is not that the Spirit is divided; each believer receives what God gives of his Spirit (compare 3:24).

decisions.choice: has given: given and still possessed
decisions.reason: The perfect says the gift was given and remains with us.

decisions.choice: from his own Spirit (B); his Spirit (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the sense of sharing (meaning decision m3); Readable says simply that God has given his Spirit, which the share does not contradict.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God (meaning decision m2).

records.heading: Remaining in God

records.source: καὶ ἡμεῖς τεθεάμεθα καὶ μαρτυροῦμεν ὅτι ὁ πατὴρ ἀπέσταλκεν τὸν υἱὸν σωτῆρα τοῦ κόσμου.
records.gloss: And we have seen and testify that the Father has sent the Son [as] Savior of the world.
pieces: We have seen it with our own eyes, and we testify that the Father has sent the Son as Savior of the world.

L.14: And we have seen and testify that the Father has sent the Son [as] Savior of the world.

R.14: We have seen this with our own eyes, and we tell others about it: the Father sent the Son to be the Savior of the world.

decisions.choice: we have seen: the eyewitnesses saw the Son
alternatives: all believers have seen, with the eyes of faith
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 1:1 ("what we have looked at") and John 1:14 ("we have seen his glory"). No one has seen God (4:12), but the witnesses saw the Son he sent.

decisions.choice: testify: give witness, as those who saw
decisions.reason: As in 1:2 and John 1:7. The present tense: they go on bearing witness.

decisions.choice: Savior of the world: the one who saves people from every nation
decisions.reason: Key term. The Samaritans give Jesus this title in John 4:42. The world here is humanity, which the Son came to save (John 3:17); compare 2:2, "the whole world".

decisions.choice: it / this with our own eyes
decisions.reason: English needs an object for "seen"; "with our own eyes" gives the eyewitness sense of meaning decision m1.

decisions.choice: tell others about it
decisions.reason: "Testify" sounds like a courtroom to a young reader; Readable says what the witnesses do.

records.source: ὃς ἐὰν ὁμολογήσῃ ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, ὁ θεὸς ἐν αὐτῷ μένει καὶ αὐτὸς ἐν τῷ θεῷ.
records.gloss: Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God in him remains and he in God.
pieces: When anyone confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God remains in {{gender:them|him}}, and {{gender:they remain|he remains}} in God.

L.15: Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God remains in {{gender:them|him}} and {{gender:they|he}} in God.

R.15: If people openly say that Jesus is the Son of God, God remains in them, and they remain in God.

decisions.choice: whoever confesses: anyone at all who makes this confession
decisions.reason: The general relative with the subjunctive covers every case. The confession is a real one, matched by life (compare 4:20).

decisions.choice: Jesus is the Son of God: the confession that marks those who belong to God
decisions.reason: The same confession is the test in 2:22-23 and 5:5, 10; it answers those who deny that Jesus is the Christ, the Son.

decisions.choice: God remains in them and they in God: a mutual indwelling
decisions.reason: As in 4:13 and 4:16, and in John 6:56 and 15:4.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}; {{gender:they|he}}
decisions.reason: The person meant is anyone who confesses. Readable uses the plural and needs no setting.

decisions.choice: openly say
decisions.reason: As in 4:2.

records.source: καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐγνώκαμεν καὶ πεπιστεύκαμεν τὴν ἀγάπην ἣν ἔχει ὁ θεὸς ἐν ἡμῖν.
records.gloss: And we have known and have believed the love that has God in us.
pieces: We ourselves have come to know the love God has for us, and we believe it.

L.16: And we have known and have believed the love that God has in us.

R.16: We know the love God has for us, and we believe in it.

decisions.choice: we ourselves: the witnesses of 4:14, with all who confess (4:15)
decisions.reason: The emphatic pronoun links back to the witnesses; the "we" here seems wide enough to include every believer.

decisions.choice: have come to know and have come to believe: and still do
decisions.reason: Both verbs are perfect: a knowledge and a belief reached and still held. Peter joins the same two verbs in John 6:69.

decisions.choice: for us: the love God has toward us, shown in our case
decisions.reason: As in 4:9, the phrase names those to whom God's love is directed and in whom it is at work.

decisions.choice: believe: accept as true and rely on
decisions.reason: Key term. Here the object is God's love: to believe it is to accept it and rest on it.

decisions.choice: come to know the love ..., and we believe it
alternatives: have come to know and believe the love
decisions.reason: English joins the two verbs to one object awkwardly; Balanced and Readable name the love once and come back to it with "it".

records.source: Ὁ θεὸς ἀγάπη ἐστίν, καὶ ὁ μένων ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ ἐν τῷ θεῷ μένει καὶ ὁ θεὸς ἐν αὐτῷ μένει.
records.gloss: The God love is, and the [one] remaining in the love in the God remains and the God in him remains.
pieces: God is love. Whoever remains in love remains in God, and God remains in {{gender:them|him}}.

L.16: God is love, and the one who remains in love remains in God, and God remains in {{gender:them|him}}.

R.16: God is love. Anyone who keeps on loving remains in God, and God remains in {{gender:them|him}}.

decisions.choice: God is love: as in 4:8
decisions.reason: See the decision at 4:8 on what the sentence says and does not say. Here it grounds the promise that follows: to remain in love is to remain in God.

decisions.choice: remains in love: goes on living in the love God has shown, by loving others
alternatives: remains in God's love for us, without reference to our love
decisions.reason: The love is the love God has for us (4:16a), lived out in love for one another (4:12). The two belong together.

decisions.choice: remains in God and God in them: the mutual indwelling of 4:13, 15
decisions.reason: The verb comes three times in one sentence.

decisions.choice: keeps on loving
decisions.reason: "Remain in love" can sound like a feeling one stays in; Readable gives the sense of meaning decision m2.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: The person meant is anyone who remains in love.

records.heading: Love has no room for fear

records.source: ἐν τούτῳ τετελείωται ἡ ἀγάπη μεθ’ ἡμῶν, ἵνα παρρησίαν ἔχωμεν ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῆς κρίσεως, ὅτι καθὼς ἐκεῖνός ἐστιν καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐσμεν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ τούτῳ.
records.gloss: In this has been perfected the love with us, so that confidence we may have in the day of the judgment, because just as that one is also we are in the world this.
pieces: In this way love has been brought to completion among us, so that we may have confidence on the day of judgment, for just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is, so are we in this world.

L.17: In this love has been perfected with us, so that we may have boldness on the day of judgment, because just as that one is, so also are we in this world.

R.17: This is how love has done its full work among us, so that we can be confident on the day of judgment. For even now, here in this world, we are as Jesus is.

decisions.choice: in this: in our remaining in love and God in us (4:16), with the goal that we have confidence
alternatives: points ahead: love is brought to completion in this, that we have confidence
points ahead to the last clause: in being as he is
decisions.reason: ἐν τούτῳ usually points ahead in this letter, and the ἵνα clause could say what "this" is. But a purpose clause rarely explains "this", so many read it as pointing back to 4:16. The sense is close either way: love brought to its goal gives confidence.

decisions.choice: with us: among us, in our life together
decisions.reason: The preposition means "with": love at work in the community.

decisions.choice: confidence: freedom to stand before someone without fear or shame
decisions.reason: The word first meant freedom of speech. In this letter it is the confidence of a child before God, now (3:21; 5:14) and when Christ appears (2:28).

decisions.choice: that one: Jesus
decisions.reason: In this letter ἐκεῖνος used of a person regularly means Jesus (2:6; 3:3, 5, 7, 16).

decisions.choice: as he is, so are we: believers already share his standing with the Father and live as he lived, while still in this world
alternatives: we are sinless as he is
decisions.reason: Jesus is loved by the Father and remains in him; those who remain in love share that standing, and are to walk as he walked (2:6; 3:2-3). This is why they need not fear the judgment. The letter does not claim they are without sin (1:8) or equal to him.

decisions.choice: boldness (L); confidence (B); be confident (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the root sense of free, bold speech; Balanced and Readable give its sense here (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: has been perfected (L); has been brought to completion (B); has done its full work (R)
decisions.reason: As in 4:12.

decisions.choice: Jesus; even now, here in this world
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus (meaning decision m4) and stresses that this is true already, before the day of judgment.

records.source: φόβος οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ, ἀλλ’ ἡ τελεία ἀγάπη ἔξω βάλλει τὸν φόβον, ὅτι ὁ φόβος κόλασιν ἔχει, ὁ δὲ φοβούμενος οὐ τετελείωται ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ.
records.gloss: Fear not is in the love, but the perfect love out casts the fear, because the fear punishment has, and the [one] fearing not has been perfected in the love.
pieces: Love has no room for fear; instead, complete love throws fear out, because fear has to do with punishment, and anyone who is afraid has not been brought to completion in love.

L.18: Fear is not in love, but perfect love casts out fear, because fear has punishment, and the one who fears has not been perfected in love.

R.18: Where there is love, there is no fear. Love that is complete pushes fear out. Fear comes from expecting to be punished. So if someone is afraid, love has not yet done its full work in {{gender:them|him}}.

decisions.choice: fear: dread of God's judgment and punishment
decisions.reason: The context is the day of judgment (4:17). The fear driven out is the dread of someone who expects to be condemned, not the reverent fear of God that Scripture commends elsewhere (Proverbs 1:7; 1 Peter 2:17).

decisions.choice: complete: love that has reached its goal
decisions.reason: The adjective belongs to the same word family as "brought to completion" in 4:12, 17 and at the end of this verse.

decisions.choice: fear has to do with punishment: it looks ahead to punishment and already feels its weight
decisions.reason: κόλασιν means punishment (as in Matthew 25:46). Fear is bound up with it: the one who fears is thinking of punishment and already suffers from the thought. The older rendering "torment" takes the second half of this.

decisions.choice: the one who fears has not been brought to completion in love: love has not yet reached its goal in them
decisions.reason: The perfect describes a present state. Fear shows that God's love has not yet done its full work; it is a call to rest in that love, not a verdict.

decisions.choice: Love has no room for fear (B); Where there is love, there is no fear (R)
alternatives: There is no fear in love
decisions.reason: Both keep the sense of the opening clause in natural wording.

decisions.choice: perfect, perfected (L); complete, brought to completion (B); complete, done its full work (R)
decisions.reason: As in 4:12 and 4:17.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: "Someone" is anyone; the pronoun takes the gender setting. Literal and Balanced need no pronoun.

records.source: ἡμεῖς ἀγαπῶμεν, ὅτι αὐτὸς πρῶτος ἠγάπησεν ἡμᾶς.
records.gloss: We love, because he first loved us.
pieces: We love because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loved us first.

L.19: We love, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} first loved us.

R.19: We love because God loved us first.

decisions.choice: we love: a statement
alternatives: let us love (a call, as in 4:7)
decisions.reason: In the present tense the statement and the call have the same form. The ὅτι clause gives a reason, which suits a statement of where our love comes from, but a call is possible.

decisions.choice: we love, with no object (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: The oldest manuscripts, including Codex Alexandrinus and Codex Vaticanus, have no object. Codex Sinaiticus adds "God", and most later manuscripts add "him". The additions narrow the love to love for God; without them it includes love for one another, which 4:20-21 goes on to speak of. A reviewer must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: he first: God's love comes first and makes ours possible
decisions.reason: As in 4:10: not that we loved God, but that he loved us. αὐτὸς means God.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God (meaning decision m3).

records.source: ἐάν τις εἴπῃ ὅτι Ἀγαπῶ τὸν θεόν, καὶ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ μισῇ, ψεύστης ἐστίν· ὁ γὰρ μὴ ἀγαπῶν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ ὃν ἑώρακεν, τὸν θεὸν ὃν οὐχ ἑώρακεν οὐ δύναται ἀγαπᾶν.
records.gloss: If anyone says, I love God, and the brother of him hates, a liar he is; for the [one] not loving the brother of him whom he has seen, God whom not he has seen not is able to love.
pieces: If someone says, "I love God," but hates {{gender:a brother or sister|his brother}}, that person is a liar. For anyone who does not love {{gender:a brother or sister|his brother}}, whom {{gender:they have|he has}} seen, is not able to love God, whom {{gender:they have|he has}} not seen.

L.20: If anyone says, "I love God," and hates {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}}, {{gender:they are|he is}} a liar; for the one who does not love {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}}, whom {{gender:they have|he has}} seen, cannot love God, whom {{gender:they have|he has}} not seen.

R.20: Suppose someone says, "I love God," but hates a fellow believer. That person is a liar. People who do not love a fellow believer they have seen cannot love God, whom they have never seen.

decisions.choice: brother: a fellow believer, man or woman, a member of God's family
decisions.reason: In this letter the brother is a fellow child of God (3:10-17; 5:1-2). The word is masculine in form but covers sisters as well. Love for all people is not denied, but this is the immediate sense.

decisions.choice: hate: refuse love and help, not only feel dislike
decisions.reason: In 3:15-17 hating a brother is set beside closing one's heart to a brother in need.

decisions.choice: a liar: one whose claim is contradicted by life
decisions.reason: As in 1:6 and 2:4: a claim to know or love God is tested by how one lives.

decisions.choice: an argument from the easier to the harder: the seen brother and the unseen God
decisions.reason: If one does not love the person one can see, love for the God no one has seen (4:12) is impossible. The perfect "has seen" means seen and known.

decisions.choice: cannot love (SBLGNT)
alternatives: how can he love God? (πῶς instead of οὐ)
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts, including some early ones and most later ones, put the end as a question, "how can he love God...?"; others, including Codex Vaticanus, have the statement. The meaning is the same. A reviewer must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}}; {{gender:a brother or sister|his brother}}; {{gender:they are|he is}}; {{gender:they have|he has}}
decisions.reason: The brother may be a man or a woman (meaning decision m1), and the speaker is anyone. Balanced uses "that person", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: a fellow believer
decisions.reason: Readable says who is meant (meaning decision m1); the wording is already inclusive and needs no setting.

decisions.choice: is not able to love
decisions.reason: The verb means "is not able"; Balanced says so in full, Literal and Readable use "cannot".

records.source: καὶ ταύτην τὴν ἐντολὴν ἔχομεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ, ἵνα ὁ ἀγαπῶν τὸν θεὸν ἀγαπᾷ καὶ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And this the commandment we have from him, that the [one] loving God love also the brother of him.
pieces: And this is the command we have received from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: the one who loves God is to love {{gender:a brother or sister|his brother}} as well.

L.21: And this commandment we have from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: that the one who loves God should love {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}} also.

R.21: God has given us this command: anyone who loves God has to love other believers too.

decisions.choice: from him: from God, who gave the command through Jesus
decisions.reason: God is the subject of 4:20, and in 3:23 the command to love one another is God's. Jesus gave it to his disciples (John 13:34), so the two are not in tension.

decisions.choice: that: gives what the command says
decisions.reason: The clause states the content of the command.

decisions.choice: brother: a fellow believer, man or woman
decisions.reason: As in 4:20.

decisions.choice: {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}}; {{gender:a brother or sister|his brother}}
decisions.reason: As in 4:20.

decisions.choice: God has given us; other believers
alternatives: we have from him; his brother
decisions.reason: Readable names God (meaning decision m1) and uses an inclusive plural that needs no setting.

decisions.choice: commandment (L); command (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Command" is the everyday word.
